Data Storage & External Services

The web application reads job records, facets, suggestions, and ZIP-code coordinates from two Azure AI Search indexes named nycjobs and zipcodes. The importer loads index schemas and document JSON from local files and sends create, delete, and upload requests to the configured Azure AI Search service. No relational database or cache is configured in the inspected application files.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The job-search website uses ASP.NET MVC controllers and a dedicated JobsSearch class to mediate access to Azure AI Search.
  • Search and location lookup are backed by separate job and ZIP-code indexes.
  • A standalone console application provides an offline-style bulk index recreation and data upload path using local schema and JSON files.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob and NYCJobLookup are response models returned by the search and lookup actions. They are mutable C# classes; no dedicated request-body DTOs or immutable contract types were identified. Search inputs are supplied as query and route parameters. The importer transmits index schemas and document payloads as JSON files. No OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL, or protobuf contract files were found.

Communication Patterns

The browser calls MVC actions over HTTP. HomeController makes synchronous direct calls through JobsSearch to Azure AI Search for queries and document lookup; no message broker, service discovery, gateway aggregation, retry policy, circuit breaker, or explicit timeout policy was identified. The importer uses synchronous HttpClient calls via AzureSearchHelper to the Azure Search REST API.

The application configuration does not show API authentication, authorization, or an application-level TLS enforcement policy. The search service integration is configured to use the HTTPS Azure Search endpoint; client-to-application transport security depends on deployment configuration not present here.

Core Business Workflows

The application helps users discover New York City job postings by text, title, posting type, salary, and location. A separate utility reloads the job and ZIP-code search data from local files.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
Job PostingNYCJobsWeb / Job SearchPublic employment listing presented to job seekersAssociated with an agency, posting and salary details, and optional geographic coordinates
ZIP CodeNYCJobsWeb / Location SearchPostal area used to find coordinates for distance-based searchesSupplies a geographic point used to constrain job searches
Search ResultNYCJobsWeb / Job SearchA matching job document returned from the search indexIncluded in a job search response with facets and total count

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob Search and Location SearchNo persistent ownership; reads job postings and ZIP-code documentsAzure AI Search nycjobs and zipcodes indexes
AzureSearchBackupRestoreSearch Data ImportNo domain ownership; provisions and populates indexesAzure AI Search and local schemas/JSON files

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search Job Postings

  1. A visitor enters a search term and optional facets, sort order, page, and location criteria.
  2. An empty search term is converted to a wildcard search.
  3. If a distance limit is selected, the application looks up the supplied ZIP code and obtains its coordinates.
  4. The application queries the job index with the term, selected facets, sort order, and optional distance filter.
  5. The results, facets, and total count are returned together to the client.

Workflow 2: Reload Search Index Data

  1. An operator starts the console importer with the target search service configured.
  2. For each of the zipcodes and nycjobs indexes, the importer attempts to delete the index, creates it from the matching local schema, and submits the matching JSON documents.
  3. The importer reports request errors to the console. No transactional rollback or automatic retry is implemented.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The web application uses ZIP-code documents to obtain coordinates, then applies those coordinates to a separate job-index search. This is an intra-application composition across two indexes; no distinct backend service aggregation, message exchange, or fallback path was identified. During reloading, the console utility is the writer for the same two indexes that the web application reads.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Visitor participant Web as "Job Search" participant ZipIndex as "ZIP Code Index" participant JobIndex as "Job Posting Index" Visitor->>Web: Search jobs with optional location and filters alt Search term is blank Web->>Web: Use wildcard query else Search term provided Web->>Web: Keep requested search term end opt Distance limit selected Web->>ZipIndex: Find coordinates for ZIP code alt ZIP code result found ZipIndex-->>Web: Return location coordinates Web->>JobIndex: Search within requested distance else No matching ZIP-code document ZipIndex-->>Web: No usable coordinates Note over Web: Empty coordinates are passed into the distance filter Web->>JobIndex: Search using requested filters end end opt No distance limit selected Web->>JobIndex: Search by text and selected filters end JobIndex-->>Web: Matching jobs, facets, and count Web-->>Visitor: Display search results

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A blank query is interpreted as a wildcard so users can browse all indexed postings.
  • A ZIP-code lookup is performed only when a positive distance limit is requested.
  • Salary-range filters represent an interval starting at the selected amount and ending 50,000 above it.
  • Supported ordering choices include featured, descending salary, ascending salary, and most recent posting.
  • The featured ordering uses the index scoring profile, including posting freshness, featured tags, and distance.
  • Search and import failures are reported through console output or null search results; no retry, compensation, transaction, or audit workflow was identified.
  • No role-based or resource-level business authorization checks were identified in the inspected workflow code.

Version & Compatibility Risks

Both projects target older .NET Framework versions (4.7.2 and 4.5), while the web stack includes ASP.NET MVC 5.2.2 and older front-end libraries. The importer targets .NET Framework 4.5 and uses Newtonsoft.Json 9.0.1. The application will require compatibility review and likely framework and package upgrades before moving to modern .NET.

Notable Observations

  • The web project and importer use different Newtonsoft.Json versions (10.0.3 and 9.0.1).
  • The web project combines the modern Azure.Search.Documents client with older Microsoft REST client packages.
  • The application includes multiple runtime support packages that are typically used to backfill newer APIs on .NET Framework.
  • The package manifests declare dependencies but no test-scoped packages.

No shared relational database, cross-service database access, CQRS implementation, or transactional data boundary was identified.
